arxiv-2105-05641.title: How Reliable are Model Diagnostics?
arxiv-2105-05641.creator: Vamsi Aribandi, Yi Tay, Donald Metzler
arxiv-2105-05641.description: Abstract In the pursuit of a deeper understanding of a model’s behaviour, there is recent impetus for developing suites of probes aimed at diagnosing models beyond simple metrics like accuracy or BLEU. This paper takes a step back and asks an important and timely question: how reliable are these diagnostics in providing insight into models and training setups?

arxiv-2203-13706.title: Some Examples of Bicrossed Products with the Rapid Decay Property
arxiv-2203-13706.creator: Hua Wang
arxiv-2203-13706.description: Abstract We consider bicrossed products obtained by twisting compact semi-direct products by a suitable finite subgroup. Under some restriction, we give a practical criterion for the discrete dual of such bicrossed products to have the rapid decay property (property (RD)). Using this theory, we construct some examples of discrete quantum groups with (RD) but do not grow polynomially.

arxiv-2301-01337.title: Low-latency parameter inference enabled by a Gaussian likelihood approximation for RIFT
arxiv-2301-01337.creator: A. B. Yelikar, V. Delfavero, R. O’Shaughnessy
arxiv-2301-01337.description: Abstract Rapid identification, characterization, and localization of gravitational waves from binary compact object mergers can enable well-informed follow-on multimessenger observations. In this work, we investigate a small modification to the RIFT parameter inference pipeline to enable extremely low-latency inference, tested here for nonprecessing sources.

arxiv-2306-17030.title: SkiROS2: A skill-based Robot Control Platform for ROS
arxiv-2306-17030.creator: Matthias Mayr, Francesco Rovida, Volker Krueger
arxiv-2306-17030.description: Abstract The need for autonomous robot systems in both the service and the industrial domain is larger than ever. In the latter, the transition to small batches or even “batch size 1” in production created a need for robot control system architectures that can provide the required flexibility. Such architectures must not only have a sufficient knowledge integration framework.

arxiv-2312-06493.title: On One Dimensional Advection - Diffusion Equation with Variable Diffusivity
arxiv-2312-06493.creator: Eeshwar Prasad Poudel, Pitambar Acharya, Jeevan Kafle, Shreeram Khadka
arxiv-2312-06493.description: Abstract In this paper, we address a time-dependent one-dimensional linear advection-diffusion equation with Dirichlet homogeneous boundary conditions. The equation is solved both analytically, using separation of variables, and numerically, employing the finite difference method. The computational output includes three dimensional (3D) plots for solutions, focusing on pollutants such as Ammonia, Carbon monoxide, Carbon dioxide, and Sulphur dioxide.

arxiv-2409-07963.title: Nanoporosity imaging by positronium lifetime tomography DOI: www.doiToFillIn.com
arxiv-2409-07963.creator: K. Dulski, E. Beyene, N. Chug, C. Curceanu, E. Czerwiński, M. Das, M. Gorgol, B. Jasińska, K. Kacprzak, Ł. Kapłon, G. Korcyl, T. Kozik, K. Kubat, D. Kumar, E. Lisowski, F. Lisowski, J. Mędrala-Sowa, S. Niedźwiecki, P. Pandey, S. Parzych, E. Perez del Rio, M. Rädler, S. Sharma, M. Skurzok, K. Tayefi,
arxiv-2409-07963.description: Abstract Positron Annihilation Lifetime Spectroscopy (PALS) is a well-established non-destructive technique used for nanostructural characterization of porous materials. It is based on the annihilation of a positron and an electron. Mean positron lifetime in the material depends on the free voids size and molecular environment, allowing the study of porosity and structural transitions in the nanometer scale.

pmc-11319222.title: Successful immunosuppressive drug‐free immune tolerance induction in hemophilia B with inhibitor and anaphylaxis to factor IX: A case report
pmc-11319222.creator: Ángeles Palomo Bravo, Rosario Prieto Bonilla, Daniel Bardan Rebollar, Francisco José López‐Jaime, Ihosvany Fernández‐Bello
pmc-11319222.description: Key Clinical MessageRecommendations advise factor IX desensitization before immune tolerance induction in severe hemophilia B, supported by immunosuppression. A child with inhibitor and anaphylaxis to factor IX showed successful immunosuppression‐free immune tolerance induction using very low and slowly increasing doses of a factor IX extended‐half‐life product. Immune tolerance to factor IX based on this protocol merits further study.

pmc-11632275.title: Hydrodissection for pericardial adhesion in percutaneous epicardial ventricular tachycardia ablation
pmc-11632275.creator: Yoshimi Onishi, Taku Asano, Shuhei Arai, Yuya Nakamura, Toshiro Shinke
pmc-11632275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Epicardial ablation in patients with pericardial adhesions is challenging. This case is the first report of successful epicardial ventricular tachycardia ablation by combining hydrodissection with the previously reported blunt dissection techniques for pericardial adhesions. This approach demonstrates a promising technique for managing similar cases where traditional methods may fail, providing a safer and more effective solution for epicardial ablation in patients with pericardial adhesions. Pericardial adhesions pose significant challenges to epicardial ventricular tachycardia (VT) catheter ablation (CA).

pmc-12738839.title: Dramatic expansion of bimodal redox window of indigo by two-electron redox processes
pmc-12738839.creator: Monojit Roy, Shyamali Maji, Vikramjeet Singh, Dhananjay Dey, Debashis Adhikari
pmc-12738839.description: Indigo is an extremely popular molecule in dye industry, however, its use in photochemical transformations is surprisingly scarce. This report explores its photocatalytic activity over an unusually wide excited-state redox window, spanning over 5.98 V. The dye molecule exhibits bimodality and proves itself as a simultaneous super-reductant and -oxidant.

pmc-12804932.title: Sociodemographic variation and childhood predictors of showing love and care for others in 22 countries
pmc-12804932.creator: Matthew T Lee, Renae Wilkinson, Katelyn N G Long, Brendan W Case, James L Ritchie-Dunham, Matt Bradshaw, R Noah Padgett, Byron R Johnson, Tyler J VanderWeele
pmc-12804932.description: Showing love and care for other people is a vital aspect of human relationships. However, little is known about how levels of love/care expression differ across cultures and across sociodemographic groups within those different cultures, or about the potential childhood antecedents that are associated with love/care expression in adulthood.

pmc-12986670.title: Mushroom-Derived Hydrophobins for Antifouling and Interface Preservation in Chemosensors
pmc-12986670.creator: Nardos F. Bisrat, Bethany R. Finnefrock, Matthew D. Gacura, Longyan Chen, Davide Piovesan
pmc-12986670.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Surface fouling remains a critical challenge for medical devices and chemosensor systems operating in biological environments, where nonspecific adsorption of proteins, cells, and microorganisms can lead to signal drift, reduced sensitivity, and shortened device lifetime. Conventional antifouling strategies rely primarily on synthetic hydrophilic polymer coatings, such as polyethylene glycol and polyvinylpyrrolidone, which are effective but face limitations related to long-term stability, thickness, and compatibility with surface-sensitive sensing modalities.

pmc-13087529.title: Causal Exposures of Immune Cells in Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorders: A Mendelian Randomization Study and Flow Cytometry Analysis
pmc-13087529.creator: Jingru Ren, Jianchun Wang, Zhenyu Niu, Jing Guo, Nan Zhang, Hongjun Hao, Feng Gao, Ran Liu, Zhaoxia Wang
pmc-13087529.description: BackgroundNeuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) are an immune‐mediated inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (CNS) primarily characterized by anti‐aquaporin‐4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4‐IgG)‐mediated astrocyte injury, neuroinflammation, and demyelination. However, the relationship between the disease and the immune trait from a genetic perspective still requires further confirmation.

pmc-13185520.creator: Bruno Ferraz Barbosa da Costa, Vanessa Feitosa Alves, Luísa Schertel Cassiano, Gustavo Giacomelli Nascimento, Valeska Maria Souto Paiva, Lívia Valéria Lins e Silva, Sabrina Garcia de Aquino
pmc-13185520.description: :This single-blind, randomized clinical trial evaluated the impact of a strict oral hygiene (OH) phase on self-reported halitosis and quality of life (QoL) in patients with periodontitis. This study reports a secondary analysis of a single-blind randomized controlled trial (parallel, 1:1), registered at RBR-5jmx32v.

pmc-13342945.creator: Aneela Pasha, Shahiryar Khan, Muhammad Farrukh Qazi, Benazir Balouch, Javeria Bilal Qamar, Muhammad Imran Nisar, Fyezah Jehan
pmc-13342945.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effect of antenatal interventions on infant growth from birth till 12 months of age.Patients and MethodsIn the Mumta Pregnant Women (PW) trial conducted from July 22, 2019, to February 1, 2022, PW were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to one of 4 groups: control (standard antenatal care), balanced energy protein supplementation (BEP alone), BEP/azithromycin (AZ), or BEP/nicotinamide/choline.

pmc-13574872.title: Cultural bias in large language models’ ability to follow neuroradiology guidelines
pmc-13574872.creator: Naël Bazerbachi, Raphaël Bentegeac, Giada Pistilli, Su-Hwan Kim, Philippe Amouyel, Jean-Pierre Pruvo, Lotfi Hacein-Bey, Aghiles Hamroun, Grégory Kuchcinski, Bastien Le Guellec
pmc-13574872.description: ObjectivesLarge language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as decision-support tools in medical imaging. However, their ability to align with country-specific guidelines, which often diverge, remains uncertain. We set out to evaluate the geographic neutrality of three state-of-the-art LLMs—GPT-o3, Mistral Large, and DeepSeek R1—and a biomedical LLM (MedGemma 1.5 4B), when applied to neuroradiology scenarios with conflicting U.S. and non-U.S. recommendations.

pmc-13677612.title: CDK4/6 Inhibitors and Curcumin Synergistically Suppress HER2− Breast Cancer via Lethal ROS and Inhibition of Metastasis
pmc-13677612.creator: Chenyu Wang, Yiqin Zou, Chunyu Chang, Siyue Liu, Xiankun Ke, Liang Hu, Di Wang, Yukang Lu, Shiwen Luo, Sijian Huang, Yilan Hu, Wenqi Yu, Aiping Deng, Ming Yue, Jue Jiang
pmc-13677612.description: CDK4/6 inhibitors represent a key therapy for HR+/HER2− breast cancer, yet resistance and limited efficacy in triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain significant challenges. Using a self‐established drug combination prediction platform, we identified a strong synergy between the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib and the natural compound curcumin across both HR+/HER2− and TNBC models, an effect that was also observed with ribociclib.
